parts.latex: Based on the graph, what is the maximum height reached by the ball?
Based on the graph, at what TWO times is the ball at $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of its maximum height?

solutions.latex:
The maximum of the graph gives
$$\text{Maximum height} = 24 \text{ m}$$

$$\begin{aligned}\dfrac{3}{4}\text{ of maximum height} &= 24\times\dfrac{3}{4} \\ &= 18 \text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
From the graph, the ball is at 18 m when $t = 1$ and $t = 3$.
$$\therefore\ t = 1 \text{ second and } t = 3 \text{ seconds}$$
criteria: Calculates $\dfrac{3}{4}$ of the maximum height, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The object is at least 300 m high when $h \ge 300$.
$$\begin{aligned} -5t^2 + 80t &\ge 300 \\ t^2 - 16t + 60 &\le 0 &&(\text{divide by } -5,\ \text{reverse the inequality}) \\ (t-6)(t-10) &\le 0 \end{aligned}$$
The parabola $y=(t-6)(t-10)$ opens upwards, so it is at or below zero between its roots:
$$6 \le t \le 10$$
The time spent at 300 m or more is
$$10 - 6 = 4 \text{ seconds}$$
This agrees with the graph, where the curve meets $h=300$ at $t=6$ and $t=10$. This is option A.

parts.latex: Which of the following could represent the graph of $y = -x^2 + 1$?

solutions.latex:
The graph of $y=-x^2+1$ is a parabola, since $x$ is squared.

The coefficient of $x^2$ is negative, so it is concave down.

The $y$-intercept is found by letting $x=0$:
$$y=1$$
The $x$-intercepts are found by letting $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned} -x^2+1 &= 0 \\ x^2 &= 1 \\ x &= \pm 1 \end{aligned}$$
So the graph is a concave down parabola with $y$-intercept $1$ and $x$-intercepts $-1$ and $1$. Only graph C has these features (A is a line, B is exponential, D is a hyperbola).

$$\therefore\ \text{the graph is C}$$

4554.stem:
A water fountain display shoots water in a parabolic arc. The height of water above the ground, $H$, in metres, of the water as a function of time, $t$, in seconds, is given by

$H = 3 + 2t - 0.5t^2$

The graph of the equation is shown below.

\exfigure{16_q9_1}

figures.cap: graph of H against t, parabola with bold section from t=0 to t=5

parts.latex: Provide one reason why, in this context, the model $H = 3 + 2t - 0.5t^2$ only makes sense for the bold section of the graph.
Use the graph to determine when the water is at the maximum height and state the maximum height.
Use the equation to show that after 4 seconds, the height of the water is 3 metres.

solutions.latex:
Either of the following is a correct reason.

Time cannot be negative.

The water does not pass through the ground.

The maximum height is $5$ m.

It occurs at $t = 2$ seconds.
criteria: Maximum height $5$ m, or time $2$ s

solutions.latex:
Substitute $t=4$ into the equation.

$$\begin{aligned} H &= 3 + 2(4) - 0.5(4)^2 \\ &= 3 + 8 - 8 \\ &= 3 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: Which of the following is a parabola?

solutions.latex:
A parabola is the graph of a quadratic $y = ax^2 + bx + c$: a smooth U-shape with one turning point and a vertical axis of symmetry.

Option A has this shape, with its vertex on the $y$-axis above the $x$-axis.

Option B is a straight line, option C is an exponential curve (it has a horizontal asymptote and no turning point) and option D is a cubic curve (it has a point of inflection and is not symmetric about the $y$-axis).

So the parabola is option A.

4472.stem:
A publisher sells a book for $\$10$. At this price, 5000 copies of the book will be sold and the revenue raised will be $5000 \times 10 = \$50\,000$.

The publisher is considering increasing the price of the book. For every dollar the price of the book is increased, the publisher will sell 50 fewer copies of the book.

If the publisher charges $(10 + x)$ dollars for each book, a quadratic model for the revenue raised, $R$, from selling the books is

$$R = -50x^2 + 4500x + 50\,000.$$

A graph of this quadratic model for revenue is shown. A dashed line is used for values of $x$ which are not relevant to the practical context of this problem.

\exfigure{38_q35_1}

figures.cap: parabola of revenue R against x, roots at -10 and 100

parts.latex: By first finding a suitable value of $x$, find the price the publisher should charge for each book to maximise the revenue raised from sales of the book.
Find the value of the intercept of the parabola with the vertical axis.

solutions.latex:
The parabola is symmetric about its vertical axis of symmetry, which passes through the maximum, midway between the two $x$-intercepts. Hence the maximum revenue occurs at $x = 45$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Price} &= 10 + 45 \\ &= \$55 \end{aligned}$$
The publisher should charge $\$55$ for each book.

meta.format_note: The x-intercepts are read from the given graph (not visible); source states x=45 by symmetry.

solutions.latex: The intercept with the vertical axis occurs at $x=0$, giving $R = 50\,000$.

parts.latex:
A sheet of metal is folded to make a gutter, as shown. The cross-section of the gutter is a rectangle of width $w$ cm and height $h$ cm.

\exfigure{40_q26_1}

The area, $A \text{ cm}^2$, of the cross-section can be modelled by the quadratic formula

$$A = -0.5w^2 + 20w.$$

A graph of this model is shown.

\exfigure{40_q26_2}

Find the width and height of the rectangle which will give the greatest possible area of the cross-section.

solutions.latex:
The maximum area occurs at the highest point of the graph, where the width is $w=20$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= -0.5(20)^2+20(20) \\ &= 200 \text{ cm}^2 \end{aligned}$$
Since $A=h\times w$:
$$\begin{aligned} 200 &= h\times 20 \\ h &= 10 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{width}=20 \text{ cm}, \text{ height}=10 \text{ cm}$$
criteria: Finds correct maximum area, or equivalent merit
Finds the width corresponding to maximum area, or equivalent merit

6003.stem:
The graph of a quadratic function represented by the equation $h = t^2 - 8t + 12$ is shown.

\exfigure{5834_q20_1}

figures.cap: parabola h = t^2 - 8t + 12 with intercepts 2 and 6

parts.latex: Find the values of $t$ and $h$ at the turning point of the graph.

The graph shows $h = 12$ when $t = 0$.

What is the other value of $t$ for which $h = 12$?

solutions.latex:
The turning point lies on the axis of symmetry, midway between the $t$-intercepts $t=2$ and $t=6$.
$$t = \dfrac{2+6}{2} = 4$$
Substitute into the equation.
$$\begin{aligned} h &= 4^2 - 8 \times 4 + 12 \\ &= -4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{turning point } (4, -4)$$
criteria: Finds the correct value of $t$, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source wrote $\frac{6+2}{2}$; intercepts 2 and 6 read from graph.

solutions.latex:
The axis of symmetry is $t = 4$, and $t = 0$ is $4$ units to its left.
$$t = 4 + 4 = 8$$
$$\therefore\ t = 8$$

The graph of a parabola with equation $y = -1.5x^2 + 15x - 31.5$ is shown.

parts.latex: What is the $x$-value of the intercept at point $A$?
What is the $y$-value of the turning point?

solutions.latex:
From the graph, the turning point is at $x = 5$ and point $A$ is $2$ units to the right of it (parabola symmetry).
$$\begin{aligned} x &= 5 + 2 \\ &= 7 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ x = 7$$

Substitute the turning point's $x$-value, $x = 5$, into the equation.
$$\begin{aligned} y &= -1.5 \times 5^2 + 15 \times 5 - 31.5 \\ &= 6 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ y = 6$$
